In the archetypal sacrifice, however, because of its own explicit word, it would be understood according to the sequence.

5.1.s: mantratas tu virodhe syāt prayogarūpasāmarthyāt tasmād utpattideśaḥ saḥ /
5.1.d: मन्त्रतस् तु विरोधे स्यात् प्रयोगरूपसामर्थ्यात् तस्माद् उत्पत्तिदेशः सः ।
5.1.m: In case of conflict, however, it follows the Vedic recitation, because of the capacity of the form of performance; therefore, that is the place of origination.
In the ectypal sacrifice, because of that statement, it should follow the principal rite.
Or in case of conflict, it should be as in the archetypal sacrifice, because of following the archetype.

5.1.s: vikṛtiḥ prakṛtidharmatvāt tatkālā syād yathā śiṣṭam /
5.1.d: विकृतिः प्रकृतिधर्मत्वात् तत्काला स्याद् यथा शिष्टम् ।
5.1.m: The ectypal sacrifice, because of sharing the properties of the archetypal sacrifice, should share its time, as instructed.

5.1.s: api vā kramakālasaṃyuktā sadyaḥ kriyeta tatra vidher anumānāt prakṛtidharmalopaḥ syāt /
5.1.d: अपि वा क्रमकालसंयुक्ता सद्यः क्रियेत तत्र विधेर् अनुमानात् प्रकृतिधर्मलोपः स्यात् ।
5.1.m: Or rather, being connected with order and time, it should be performed immediately on the same day; because of inferring an injunctive rule there, there would be loss of the properties of the archetypal sacrifice.
Because subsidiary elements share the time of the principal rite, upon postponement it would be as stated.
Or, because of connection, beginning with that and ending with that, upon advancement [it would be similarly adjusted].
and because of non-contradiction of verbal testimony.

5.1.s: asaṃyogāt tu vaikṛtaṃ tad eva pratikṛṣyeta.
5.1.d: असंयोगात् तु वैकृतं तद् एव प्रतिकृष्येत।
5.1.m: Due to non-connection, however, that ectypal element alone should be advanced.
And an incidental element should not be postponed, due to non-connection.
The Sāntapanīyā oblation, however, should defer the Agnihotra, just as in the case of the pressing of Soma, because of ritual defect.
However, there should be no deferral, because of the absence of a connection.
And because the occasioning condition has occurred.
The deferral of the pressing is due to a direct connection.
And the Ṣoḍaśin cup [is deferred] on account of its connection with the Ukthya.

5.2.s: sannipāte prādhānānām ekaikasya guṇānāṃ sarvakarma syāt /
5.2.d: सन्निपाते प्राधानानाम् एकैकस्य गुणानां सर्वकर्म स्यात् ।
5.2.m: When principal rites concur, all operations of the subsidiaries should be performed for each one [in turn].
Or rather, [each operation should be performed] of one identical type for all [together], because an order has been established.
And with regard to the handfuls, the potsherds, the cut portions, anointing, smearing, shaving, and purifying, [the action is performed] with one [at a time].
However, all [should be performed together], because they serve a single purpose, and because these are subsidiary qualities to that [purpose].

5.2.s: saṃyukte tu prakramāt tadaṅgaṃ syād itarasya tadarthatvāt /
5.2.d: संयुक्ते तु प्रक्रमात् तदङ्गं स्याद् इतरस्य तदर्थत्वात् ।
5.2.m: When, however, it is connected [to another item], that should be its subsidiary by virtue of commencement, because the other serves its purpose.
By virtue of direct scriptural statement, however, the anointing and subsequent acts should extend up to the girding.
There may be no interruption, or it may happen on account of a specific cause, just like the increase of vessels.
Or rather not, because it is caused by the Vedic text; the other is a mere analogy, while the multiplication of vessels is due to purpose.
In a group of sacrificial animals, one should finish [the acts] for each respective animal, because the animal is a single unit.
Or rather, [they should be performed together] on account of the recipient deities, because the sacrificial action is one.
And because the Vedic recitation has a purposeful meaning.
When there are different seeds, there should be a single mortar, on account of its capacity.
Or there should be an increase [of mortars], because the order is regulated, since it serves that purpose.
Or there should be one [mortar], because of the generation of rice grains, since striking serves that purpose.

5.2.d: विकारे त्व् अनूयाजानां पात्रभेदो ऽर्थभेदात् स्यात् ।
5.2.m: In a modified rite of the after-offerings, however, there should be a distinction of vessels, on account of the distinction of purpose.

5.2.s: prakṛteḥ pūrvoktatvād apūrvam ante syān na hy acoditasya śeṣāmnānam /
5.2.d: प्रकृतेः पूर्वोक्तत्वाद् अपूर्वम् अन्ते स्यान् न ह्य् अचोदितस्य शेषाम्नानम् ।
5.2.m: Because the archetypal sacrifice is stated first, the non-archetypal element should come at the end; for the mention of a subsidiary does not belong to what has not been enjoined.

5.2.s: mukhyānantaryamātreyas tena tulyaśrutitvād aśabdatvāt prākṛtānāṃ vyavāyaḥ syāt /
5.2.d: मुख्यानन्तर्यमात्रेयस् तेन तुल्यश्रुतित्वाद् अशब्दत्वात् प्राकृतानां व्यवायः स्यात् ।
5.2.m: Ātreya holds that it must immediately succeed the primary rite; since it has equal direct scriptural statement with it, and because they are not directly declared, there would be an intervention of the archetypal elements.
Bādarāyaṇa, however, holds that it comes at the end, because those [archetypal elements] are expressed by words designating the principal rite.
And likewise there is textual evidence for another purpose.

5.2.s: kṛtadeśāt tu pūrveṣāṃ sa deśaḥ syāt tena pratyakṣasaṃyogān nayāyamātramitarat /
5.2.d: कृतदेशात् तु पूर्वेषां स देशः स्यात् तेन प्रत्यक्षसंयोगान् नयायमात्रमितरत् ।
5.2.m: However, that should be the place of the preceding elements from their appointed place; by that there is a direct connection, whereas the other is a mere deduction.
And whatever precedes the archetypal rite [remains so].
If there is a concurrence, it should be at the end, as previously stated.

5.3.m: An addition, on account of difference of actions, would be taught for each respective item, like the clotted butter.
Or rather, because it is an all-inclusive number, a modification should be understood.
However, they should increase from their own relative textual position, because the sequence has already been established.

5.3.s: samidhyamānavatīṃ samiddhavatīṃ cāntareṇa dhāyyāḥ syur dyāvāpṛthiñyorantarālaṃ samarhaṇāt /
5.3.d: समिध्यमानवतीं समिद्धवतीं चान्तरेण धाय्याः स्युर् द्यावापृथिञ्योरन्तरालं समर्हणात् ।
5.3.m: The Dhāyyā verses should be between the verse containing the word 'being kindled' and the verse containing 'kindled', because of their appropriateness in the space between heaven and earth.
Because of the observation [of them] at the end of the Uṣṇih and Kakubh metres.

5.3.s: stomavivṛddhau vahiṣpavamāne purastāt paryāsād āgantavaḥ syus tathā hi dṛṣṭaṃ dvādaśāhe /
5.3.d: स्तोमविवृद्धौ वहिष्पवमाने पुरस्तात् पर्यासाद् आगन्तवः स्युस् तथा हि दृष्टं द्वादशाहे ।
5.3.m: When there is an increase of the Stoma in the Bahiṣpavamāna hymn, the adventitious verses should be inserted before the final triplet; for so it is seen in the Twelve-Day rite.
Even if it were a modification of it, it would be [at the end] on account of being an unprecedented insertion.
However, one should place them at the end of the two subsequent verses.
Or rather, in the Gāyatrī, Bṛhatī, and Anuṣṭubh metres, by virtue of direct scriptural statement.
The bricks relating to the cups and those of the supplementary section should be considered subsidiaries of the layer of the Soma-pressing.
Or rather, they are subsidiaries of the sacrificial rite and the fire-altar, because they are enjoined, whereas their sequence is not enjoined.
In the middle layer, however, the bricks accompanied by Brāhmaṇa passages [are placed], by virtue of direct scriptural statement.
[They are placed] prior to the space-filling brick, because that brick serves the purpose of completing [the layer].
The ritual act takes place when [the altar] is consecrated, because preparatory purifications serve that purpose.
The observances immediately follow, because they pertain to that.
And [they come] before, because an indicative textual mark is observed.
Or it is a corroborative statement, because the real purpose is present.
And because there would be a conflict with the guiding principle.

5.3.s: sañcite tv agnicid yuktaṃ prāpaṇān nimittasya /
5.3.d: सञ्चिते त्व् अग्निचिद् युक्तं प्रापणान् निमित्तस्य ।
5.3.m: When it is piled, however, the term 'one who has piled the fire-altar' is appropriate, because the occasioning condition has occurred.
Or [it takes place] at the end of the sacrificial rite, because of the absence of an injunctive rule of performance.
Because the fire-altar is designated as an action.
By virtue of the announcement at the end, one becomes consecrated, because of connection with all the consecrations.
Or they are at the end of the Iṣṭi, because they are intended for that, since their connection with the purpose is without distinction.
The order of succession among the sacrificial rites is like that among the subsidiary elements.
It could be [meaningful] for the purpose of instruction, as in the case of subsequent [rites] on account of the Sarvasvāra sacrifice.
[The phrase] 'who [sacrifices] with this' refers to the Agniṣṭoma, on account of the context of the ritual topic.
[In the phrase] 'then with another', [the reference is] to the ritual forms, on account of their proximity.
Or [the passage refers to] its base paradigm, because alteration and dispersal are not possible among equal rites.
And [it is a eulogy], because there is an absence of dispersal.

5.3.s: vidhipratyayād vā na hy akasmāt praśaṃsā syāt /
5.3.d: विधिप्रत्ययाद् वा न ह्य् अकस्मात् प्रशंसा स्यात् ।
5.3.m: Or it is an injunctive cognition; for commendation cannot arise without a cause.
Or [the reference is] to a single Stoma, on account of its connection with the sacrificial rite.
Or rather, the commendation applies to all Stomas, because the injunction is not differentiated.

5.4.m: The subversion of sequence is determined by purpose and word, because direct scriptural statement is distinctive and because purpose is primary.
In the cutting, sprinkling, and placing [of oblations], the order of succession should be determined by performance.
Or according to the presentation, because they are intended for that.
The priority of the Iṣṭi is on account of direct statement.

5.4.s: somaś caikeṣām agnayādheyasyartunakṣatrātikramavacanāt tadantenānarthakaṃ hi syāt /
5.4.d: सोमश् चैकेषाम् अग्नयाधेयस्यर्तुनक्षत्रातिक्रमवचनात् तदन्तेनानर्थकं हि स्यात् ।
5.4.m: And Soma [is prior] according to some, because of the statement regarding transgreßing the season and asterism of fire-installation; for otherwise it would be meaningless if ending with that [Iṣṭi].
And because of the statement of purpose, [the installation] does not serve that purpose without distinction.

5.4.s: ayakṣyamāṇasya ca pavamānahaviṣāṃ kālanirdeśād ānantaryād viśaṅkā syāt /
5.4.d: अयक्ष्यमाणस्य च पवमानहविषां कालनिर्देशाद् आनन्तर्याद् विशङ्का स्यात् ।
5.4.m: And regarding one who is not going to sacrifice, a doubt might arise due to proximity, because of the designation of time for the Pavamāna offerings.
The Iṣṭi is for one who will not sacrifice [with Soma]; when it is for that purpose, Soma does not come first.
On account of deferment, Soma would be [performed first] for a Brāhmaṇa.
Or rather, the Full-Moon sacrifice [is first], on account of direct scriptural connection.
Or [it is prior] because everything constitutes a single ritual action.
Or there may be an injunctive rule based on that purpose.
However, the time is determined by the context of the ritual topic.
It should take place at its own time, because there is no contradiction.
Or there is a displacement of the fire-installation, because it has all times [permitted].
The Full-Moon sacrifice is after Soma for a Brāhmaṇa, on account of direct statement.
Or it is a single [sacrifice], by the force of the word; the whole [procedure] is enjoined beforehand.
The sacrificial cake, however, [is used] in the absence of specification, because there is no recipient deity connected with that [alternative material].
No, because it has mixed deities, as in the case of the offering to Indra-Agni.

5.4.s: vikṛteḥ prakṛtikālatvāt sadyaskālottarā vikṛtis tayoḥ pratyakṣaśiṣṭatvāt /
5.4.d: विकृतेः प्रकृतिकालत्वात् सद्यस्कालोत्तरा विकृतिस् तयोः प्रत्यक्षशिष्टत्वात् ।
5.4.m: Because the modified rite shares the time of the base paradigm, the modified rite that is completed in one day takes place later, because those two are taught by direct perception.
In the case of a two-day duration, however, it proceeds according to the standard principle.
Or there could be a single time, on account of direct statement.
The modifications of the Sānnāyya and the Agnīṣomīya are performed after Soma, just like the base paradigm.
Likewise, the modifications of Soma are performed after the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices.

6.1.m: When substances are connected with an action, their connection is as subordinate elements.
But it cannot be accomplished [alone], because it is meant for that purpose.

6.1.s: pratyarthaṃ cābhisaṃyogātkarmato hy abhisambandhas tasmāt karmopadeśaḥ syāt /
6.1.d: प्रत्यर्थं चाभिसंयोगात्कर्मतो ह्य् अभिसम्बन्धस् तस्मात् कर्मोपदेशः स्यात् ।
6.1.m: And because there is connection with each purpose, the relation is indeed through action; therefore, there should be an instruction regarding action.
Because action is for the sake of the fruit, the scripture should confer ritual eligibility upon all.

6.1.s: kartur vā śrutisaṃyogād vidhiḥ kārtsnyena gamyate /
6.1.d: कर्तुर् वा श्रुतिसंयोगाद् विधिः कार्त्स्न्येन गम्यते ।
6.1.m: Or rather, because the performer has a direct scriptural connection, the injunctive rule is understood in its entirety.
Aitiśāyana holds that [the injunction] applies to men, because of the specific mention of masculine gender.
And because that is spoken of, a scriptural defect is heard in the case of one unknown.

6.1.s: jātiṃ tu bādarāyaṇo 'viśeṣāt tasmāt stry api pratīyeta jātyarthasyāviśiṣṭatvāt /
6.1.d: जातिं तु बादरायणो ऽविशेषात् तस्मात् स्त्र्य् अपि प्रतीयेत जात्यर्थस्याविशिष्टत्वात् ।
6.1.m: Bādarāyaṇa, however, holds that it refers to the class, because there is no distinction; therefore, a woman too should be understood [as eligible], because the meaning of the class is non-specific.
Because it is enjoined according to direct scriptural statement.

6.1.s: dravyavattvāt tu puṃsāṃ syād dravyasaṃyuktaṃ krayavikrayābhyām adravyatvaṃ strīṇāṃ dravyaiḥ samānayogitvāt /
6.1.d: द्रव्यवत्त्वात् तु पुंसां स्याद् द्रव्यसंयुक्तं क्रयविक्रयाभ्याम् अद्रव्यत्वं स्त्रीणां द्रव्यैः समानयोगित्वात् ।
6.1.m: However, men possess wealth; that which involves wealth is through buying and selling; women do not possess wealth, because they are treated as equal to wealth.
And likewise, there is the observation of another meaning.
Action serves that purpose because [a woman] serves that purpose.
And because she is inherently connected with the purpose.
Purchase is a mere formality.
Scripture also reveals ownership [by women].
Because both possess ownership, a single unified action should be performed on account of direct statement.
Ownership, however, is spoken of figuratively on account of being bought.
Ownership, however, is connected because of the desire for fruits.
And scripture reveals the possession of fruit.
And the establishment [of fires] belongs to two, like the sacrifice of two.

6.1.s: guṇasya tu vidhānatvāt patnyā dvitīyaśabdaḥ syāt /
6.1.d: गुणस्य तु विधानत्वात् पत्न्या द्वितीयशब्दः स्यात् ।
6.1.m: Because it is an injunction of a secondary element, the word for the second refers to the wife.
For her, only what is expressly stated [applies], such as the benediction and celibacy, because they are not identical.
[Ritual eligibility belongs to] all four social classes, because there is no distinction.

6.1.s: nirdeśād vā trayāṇāṃ syād agnyādheye 'sambandhaḥ kratuṣu brāhmaṇaśruter ity ātreyaḥ /
6.1.d: निर्देशाद् वा त्रयाणां स्याद् अग्न्याधेये ऽसम्बन्धः क्रतुषु ब्राह्मणश्रुतेर् इत्य् आत्रेयः ।
6.1.m: Or rather, by virtue of specific mention, it belongs to the three; there is no connection [for the fourth] in the establishment of the fires, and in sacrifices on account of the scriptural mention of the brāhmaṇa, so Ātreya holds.

6.1.s: nimittārthe na bādaris tasmāt sarvādhikāraṃ syāt /
6.1.d: निमित्तार्थे न बादरिस् तस्मात् सर्वाधिकारं स्यात् ।
6.1.m: Bādari [holds that] it is for the sake of the occasion, and therefore there is eligibility for all.
Or rather, because another purpose is seen, it must be understood according to the direct scriptural statement.
And in the preparatory purification, because that is primary.
Or rather, on account of the mention of Vedic study, [eligibility] should be understood as excluding Śūdras.
[we reply:] because the preparatory purification serves that purpose, the scriptural mention of the person applies to knowledge.
If it is objected that it is not so, because knowledge is specified,
[we reply that] on account of lack of Vedic learning, there would be absence in the rite.
And likewise, there is an indication of another meaning.
Of the three, [only one] endowed with wealth [has eligibility], because rites are accomplished with substance.

6.1.s: anityatvāt tu naivaṃ syād arthād dhi dravyasaṃyogaḥ /
6.1.d: अनित्यत्वात् तु नैवं स्याद् अर्थाद् धि द्रव्यसंयोगः ।
6.1.m: But it would not be so, because [wealth] is non-permanent; for the connection with substance arises from the need of the purpose.
And one deficient in limbs shares the same property.
Because at origination there is a constant connection.
There would be the exclusion of one who lacks three ancestral sages.
By virtue of explicit statement, [eligibility] belongs to the chariot-maker in the establishment of fires, because this is subsidiary to all.
Or it is proper [to consider him a Śūdra] on account of connection with the action, since the Śūdra has been prohibited.
But it cannot be so, because it is not that action.
And there would be purposelessness of the connection.
The Saudhanvanas, however, because of distinctness, should be understood from the wording of the mantra.
The 'lord of charioteers' must be a Niṣāda, by the force of the word.

6.2.m: Because each serves a single human purpose, the ritual eligibility must belong to each [person individually].

6.2.s: api cotpattisaṃyogo yathā syāt satvadaryaśanaṃ tathābhāvo vibhāge syāt /
6.2.d: अपि चोत्पत्तिसंयोगो यथा स्यात् सत्वदर्यशनं तथाभावो विभागे स्यात् ।
6.2.m: Moreover, just as there is connection at origination, so that there is eating by a virtuous man, so also in division there must be the same status.
Since there is scriptural mention of the person in the performance, one would act according to desire in the performance.
If it is objected that the scriptural statement applies to each separate purpose,

6.2.d: तादर्थ्ये न गुणार्थतानुक्ते ऽर्थान्तरत्वात् कर्तुः प्रधानभूतत्वात् ।
6.2.m: [we reply:] When that is the purpose, there is no serving a subordinate quality; when unexpressed, it is another purpose, because the agent is primary.

6.2.s: api vā kāmasaṃyoge sambandhāt prayogāyopadiśyeta pratyarthaṃ hi vidhiśrutir viṣāṇāvat /
6.2.d: अपि वा कामसंयोगे सम्बन्धात् प्रयोगायोपदिश्येत प्रत्यर्थं हि विधिश्रुतिर् विषाणावत् ।
6.2.m: Or rather, in connection with desire, it would be taught for performance because of the relation; for the injunctive rule is heard for each purpose, like the horn.
[we reply:] there is a connection with another purpose.
If it is objected that the desire for the fruit is the occasion,
However, by beginning, it becomes restricted, because commencement is the occasion for the action.
Or, because one desires the fruit, there is no restriction, just as before commencing.

6.2.s: niyamo vā tannimittatvāt kartus tatkāraṇaṃ syāt /
6.2.d: नियमो वा तन्निमित्तत्वात् कर्तुस् तत्कारणं स्यात् ।
6.2.m: Or there is a restriction, because it is caused by that; that must be the cause for the agent.
Worldly actions are like the Vedic; from them arises the knowledge concerning the person.
And even in case of transgression, the scripture applies by means of them.

6.2.s: aśāstrāt tūpasamprāptiḥ śāstraṃ syān na prakalpakaṃ tasmād arthena gamyetāprāpte śāstram arthavat /
6.2.d: अशास्त्रात् तूपसम्प्राप्तिः शास्त्रं स्यान् न प्रकल्पकं तस्माद् अर्थेन गम्येताप्राप्ते शास्त्रम् अर्थवत् ।
6.2.m: From non-scriptural sources, however, comes attainment; the scripture cannot create anew; therefore it must be understood according to the purpose; when unobtained, the scripture is purposeful.

6.2.s: pratiṣedheṣv akarmatvāt kriyā syāt pratiṣiddhānāṃ vibhaktatvād akarmaṇām /
6.2.d: प्रतिषेधेष्व् अकर्मत्वात् क्रिया स्यात् प्रतिषिद्धानां विभक्तत्वाद् अकर्मणाम् ।
6.2.m: In prohibitions, because there is non-action, there would be action of prohibited things, because non-actions are distinct.

6.2.s:
śāstrāṇāṃ tv arthavatvena puruṣārtho vidhīyate tayor
asamavāyitvāt tādarthye vidhyatikramaḥ /
6.2.d:
शास्त्राणां त्व् अर्थवत्वेन पुरुषार्थो विधीयते तयोर्
असमवायित्वात् तादर्थ्ये विध्यतिक्रमः ।
6.2.m: Because scriptures are purposeful, the human purpose is enjoined; because the two are not co-inherent, in serving that purpose there is transgression of the injunctive rule.
Those being taught in it would proceed by birth.
Or rather, because it is equal to the Veda, they would proceed by means.
Repetition is enjoined as serving the human purpose, because it is not subsidiary to an action.
When that is impossible, it follows from the purpose.
They are not taught in relation to times.
Because of the observation of indicative marks of time, there is an injunction of time.
Because they are primordial, one must proceed by traditional transmission.
For thus an indicative mark is seen.
Likewise are those employed within the sacrificial rite.
In the case of [practices] known from traditional conduct, it would be so, because they serve human purposes.
For a Brāhmaṇa, however, soma, learning, and offspring [are obligatory], because of the connection with the statement on debts.

6.3.m: Action would take place only when there is full capability, because [the sacrifice] is taught as possessing all [its factors].

6.3.s: api vāpy ekadeśe syāt pradhāne hy arthanirvṛttir guṇamātram itarat tadarthatvāt /
6.3.d: अपि वाप्य् एकदेशे स्यात् प्रधाने ह्य् अर्थनिर्वृत्तिर् गुणमात्रम् इतरत् तदर्थत्वात् ।
6.3.m: Or rather, [action] should take place even partially; for the accomplishment of the purpose lies in the principal rite, whereas the other is merely a subsidiary quality, since it is for the sake of that [principal].

6.3.s: tadakarmaṇi ca doṣas tasmāt tato viśeṣaḥ syāt pradhānenābhisambandhāt /
6.3.d: तदकर्मणि च दोषस् तस्मात् ततो विशेषः स्यात् प्रधानेनाभिसम्बन्धात् ।
6.3.m: And fault arises from non-performance of that [obligatory rite]; therefore, there is a distinction regarding that [principal rite], because of its direct connection with the fruit.

6.3.s: karmābhedaṃ tu jaiminiḥ prayogavacanaikatvāt sarveṣām upadeśaḥ syād iti /
6.3.d: कर्माभेदं तु जैमिनिः प्रयोगवचनैकत्वात् सर्वेषाम् उपदेशः स्याद् इति ।
6.3.m: Jaimini, however, [holds that there is] no difference in the action, because the injunctive statement of performance is one, so that the instruction applies to all [elements].

6.3.s: arthasya vyapavargitvād ekasyāpi prayoge syād yathā kratvantareṣu /
6.3.d: अर्थस्य व्यपवर्गित्वाद् एकस्यापि प्रयोगे स्याद् यथा क्रत्वन्तरेषु ।
6.3.m: Because the beneficial purpose terminates [with completion], [the title to perform] would apply even to a single performance, as in other sacrificial rites.
And because completion is seen even upon a transgression of an injunctive rule;
And because of the prescription of expiation;
And in the case of optional rites it would be so, because [one acts] from desire.

6.3.s: asaṃyogāt tu naivaṃ syād vidheḥ śabdapramāṇatvāt /
6.3.d: असंयोगात् तु नैवं स्याद् विधेः शब्दप्रमाणत्वात् ।
6.3.m: But it would not be so [in optional rites], because of the absence of connection [with an injunction to perform unconditionally], since an injunctive rule has verbal testimony as its means of valid cognition;
And because there is no transgression upon non-performance.
Because actions depend [on substances], there would be a division [of identity] upon a different substance.

6.3.s: api vāvyatirekād rūpaśabdāvibhāgāc ca gotvavad aikakarmyaṃ syān nāmadheyaṃ ca sattvavat /
6.3.d: अपि वाव्यतिरेकाद् रूपशब्दाविभागाच् च गोत्ववद् ऐककर्म्यं स्यान् नामधेयं च सत्त्ववत् ।
6.3.m: Or rather, because there is no difference and no distinction in form and word, there would be identity of action, like cowness; and the proper ritual designation is like [the name of] a concrete entity.
And because direct scriptural statement is the means of valid cognition, upon the absence of the prescribed [substance] there can be no introduction of another, because it is unprescribed;
Or rather, there should be introduction [of a substitute], because there is no difference in the purpose of the injunction.
The prescription in a certain instance is for the sake of a restrictive injunction.
That [prescribed substance] is obligatory, for the desire to perform pertains to that.
There is no [substitution] of recipient deity, fire, word, or action, because they are connected with a different purpose.
And in the case of the recipient deity, because [the sacrifice] is for its sake.
And [substitution of these] is prohibited; for its direct scriptural statement is without qualification.
Likewise [there is no substitution] of the ritual patron, because the fruit inheres in him, and the fruit is connected with the action.
When many [patrons] are engaged, however, one should bring in another, to avoid deficiency.
Or rather, [he is] a hired labourer, because he is paid;
And because the fruit is seen in that [original patron].
He should have his duties, because of connection with the action.
There is similarity, for the desire is to perform that [same action].
In the case of an option, however, that which has commenced [is continued], because of specification.

6.3.s: vacanāc cānyāyyam abhāve tatsāmānyena pratinidhir abhāvād itarasya /
6.3.d: वचनाच् चान्याय्यम् अभावे तत्सामान्येन प्रतिनिधिर् अभावाद् इतरस्य ।
6.3.m: And by scriptural statement, [it is] improper; upon absence [of the prescribed], a substitute [is adopted] through similarity to it, because of the absence of the other.
Not in the case of a substitute, because they are equal.
It could be so in the case of that characterized by direct scriptural statement, because of restrictiveness.
Upon procuring the primary [substance], the primary [must be used]; for the introduction [of a substitute was only] because of its absence.
When there is conflict between substance and preparatory purification, the substance [prevails], because [the purification] is for its sake.

6.3.d: अर्थद्रव्यविरोधे ऽर्थो द्रव्याभावे तदुत्पत्तेर् द्रव्याणाम् अर्थशेषत्वात् ।
6.3.m: When there is conflict between purpose and substance, the purpose [prevails], because upon the absence of the substance it is produced [by another], since substances are subsidiary to the purpose.
The injunctive rule would apply even to a single portion.

6.3.s: api vārthasya śakyatvād ekadeśena nirvartetārthānām avibhaktatvād guṇamātram itarat tadarthatvāt /
6.3.d: अपि वार्थस्य शक्यत्वाद् एकदेशेन निर्वर्तेतार्थानाम् अविभक्तत्वाद् गुणमात्रम् इतरत् तदर्थत्वात् ।
6.3.m: Or rather, because the purpose is feasible, it should be accomplished with a single portion, since purposes are undivided; the other is merely a subsidiary quality, because it is for the sake of that.

6.4.m: Upon destruction of the two cuttings, it should be from the remainder, because it is for that purpose.
Or because of specific mention, one should bring in another [substance].
Or rather, [the remaining rites] should belong to those entitled to the remainder, because they are the distinct cause.
Because of specific mention, the eating of the remainder is by others, as in the principal rite.
Or it should be by all, because of co-inherence.
The specific mention is for the sake of a subsidiary quality.
In the principal rite, it is characterized by direct scriptural statement.
Because the purpose inheres [in it], an expiation [is required] even upon [the destruction of] a part.

6.4.s: na tv aśeṣe vaiguṇyāt tadarthaṃ hi /
6.4.d: न त्व् अशेषे वैगुण्यात् तदर्थं हि ।
6.4.m: Not, however, when none is left, because of deficiency; for it is for that purpose.

6.4.s: syād vā prāptanimittatvād ataddharmo nityasaṃyogān na hitasya guṇārthenānityatvāt /
6.4.d: स्याद् वा प्राप्तनिमित्तत्वाद् अतद्धर्मो नित्यसंयोगान् न हितस्य गुणार्थेनानित्यत्वात् ।
6.4.m: Or rather, it would be [applicable], because the occasion has arisen; it does not share that duty, because of connection with what is permanent, not of that which is beneficial, since it is impermanent through being for a secondary quality.

6.4.s: guṇānāṃ ca parārthatvād vacanād vyapāśraya syāt /
6.4.d: गुणानां च परार्थत्वाद् वचनाद् व्यपाश्रय स्यात् ।
6.4.m: And because subsidiary qualities are for the sake of another, the recourse would be on account of scriptural statement.
And upon the destruction of all, it would be purposeless.
In the case of scorching, however, [the expiation] applies upon total burning, because a partial [burning] is unavoidable.
Or rather, [the performance should be completed] with another [substance], because the occasion [for substitution] is obtained from scripture.
If it is objected that it is not so, because of the word 'sacrificial offering' [applied to it],

[the reply is:] it can be so; for since [the other course] is illogical, the word 'sacrificial offering' refers to what goes into the sacrifice, because of its connection with that indicative textual mark.
[we say] no, because [the statement] is an indirect characterisation, for the mishap itself is the occasion [for the rite].
And the pouring of the oblation, pressing [of Soma], and eating [follow] the same rule.

6.4.s: ubhābhyāṃ vā na hi tayor dharmaśāstram /
6.4.d: उभाभ्यां वा न हि तयोर् धर्मशास्त्रम् ।
6.4.m: Or it applies to both, because there is no rule of duty regarding those two.
The re-establishment [of the fires applies to the sacrificial session], like the boiled rice [rite].
Or rather, it belongs to both, because of the production of the substance.
The five-cup offering, however, should be a substitute, because a substance is directly stated in scripture.
Or it is an injunction [of a new sacrifice], an injunctive rule of substance and recipient deity; for [otherwise] it would be unexpressed.
It displaces [the archetypal rite], by virtue of relative textual position.
Or it is an injunctive rule of a subsidiary element, because of the connection with an occasioning condition.
In the Viśvajit, the performance should take place when the sacrificial action has commenced;
In the connection with the calf, there should be an injunction of an observance;
or rather a time, because of the connection of what has been already produced, as previously stated;
The calf, however, would be a subsidiary element of that, because of the connection in direct scriptural statement.
and because [otherwise] it would be useless when connected with the sacrificial action;
and because of the non-utterance of its own word.
If it is time, it must be in the case of one who offers the curd-and-milk oblation, because of the connection with its indicative textual mark.
Or, because it serves the purpose of time, it should be understood as applying to both [cases];
just like the leaning of the branch on the grass-bundle.
Or it is an injunction of time, because both are present.
and because it is not for the sake of consecration of that [branch];
and because it would take place upon disconnection from that.

6.5.s: abhyudaye kālāparādhād ijyācodanā syād yathā pañcaśarāve /
6.5.d: अभ्युदये कालापराधाद् इज्याचोदना स्याद् यथा पञ्चशरावे ।
6.5.m: Upon the rising [of the moon], there should be the injunction of a sacrifice, due to the fault in time, as in the case of the five-cup offering.
and because the words have that character;
and because the repetition of the curdling agent is seen;
and because an injunction would be needed due to its novelty.
In the case of the five-cup offering [it is due to] the defect of the milk, for the other [substance] is not defective.
If it is said that the curd-and-milk oblation also is like that,
[we say] no, because that is not defective, for the occasioning condition is not qualified [by defect].
In the whisper-sacrifice, since there is no special mention, it should follow the archetypal sacrifice.
It should take place when [the grain] has been measured out, because of the connection with that.
Or [it takes place] when [the rite] has commenced, because the occasioning condition is brought about.
and similarly there is observation of another passage with this purpose.

6.5.s: anirupte 'bhyudite prākṛtībhyo nirvaped ity āśmarathyas taṇḍulabhūteṣv apanayāt /
6.5.d: अनिरुप्ते ऽभ्युदिते प्राकृतीभ्यो निर्वपेद् इत्य् आश्मरथ्यस् तण्डुलभूतेष्व् अपनयात् ।
6.5.m: If the moon rises before the grain is measured out, one should measure out for the archetypal deities: thus says Āśmarathya, because the diversion occurs when they have become husked rice.
Ālekhana, however, [holds that it is] for those who have a share above, because that causes the diversion of the recipient deities.
When it has been measured out, there is no setting aside of the handfuls, because they are subordinate to that [action];
for there is connection with the non-archetypal [deities], because of occupying their position;
and it should take place due to the absence of the other.
Or rather, because of the connection with vegetable substances, it belongs to both.
On rising halfway [through a sacrificial session], the Viśvajit [applies] after [Soma] has been purchased, because of the connection with the division;
Or [it takes place] when [the rite] has commenced, because the occasioning condition is brought about.
Regarding the measure of initiation, it is according to desire, because there is no particular specification.
The twelve-day period, however, should be [adopted], because of an indicative textual mark.
On the full moon, there is no restriction, because there is no specific rule.
But because of proximity, it should be the full moon of Caitra.
Or the full moon of Māgha, on account of the direct scriptural statement regarding the Ekāṣṭakā.
No; because of its secondary usage, for this [alone] is [so known] in the world.
And because of the accommodation when consecration is missed.

6.5.s: dīkṣākālasya śiṣṭatvād atikrame niyatānām anutkarṣaḥ prāptakālatvāt /
6.5.d: दीक्षाकालस्य शिष्टत्वाद् अतिक्रमे नियतानाम् अनुत्कर्षः प्राप्तकालत्वात् ।
6.5.m: Because the time of consecration is explicitly enjoined, upon its lapse there is no postponement of regular [rites], because their time has arrived.

6.5.s: utkarṣo vā dīkṣitatvād aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam /
6.5.d: उत्कर्षो वा दीक्षितत्वाद् अविशिष्टं हि कारणम् ।
6.5.m: Or rather there is postponement, because he has become consecrated; for the reason is unvaried.

6.5.s: tatra pratihomo na vidyate yathā pūrveṣām /
6.5.d: तत्र प्रतिहोमो न विद्यते यथा पूर्वेषाम् ।
6.5.m: In that case, there is no compensatory homa, just as with the preceding ones.
And because of prohibition, after the Avabhṛtha there is an iṣṭi.
If there were a compensatory homa, the evening Agnihotra and the like would have to be offered.
The expiation should apply universally under the title to perform, because the fault is common [to all].
Or it applies only to the context of the ritual topic, because the text is the sole cause.

6.5.s: vyāpannasyāpsu gatau yad abhojyam āryāṇāṃ tat pratīyeta /
6.5.d: व्यापन्नस्याप्सु गतौ यद् अभोज्यम् आर्याणां तत् प्रतीयेत ।
6.5.m: When spoiled [food] has gone into the water, that which is inedible to the noble should be recognized [as spoiling].
Because of the direct scriptural statement of division, no expiation exists in the case of simultaneity.
Or it may exist, because the occasion has arisen, [the distinction being] merely one of time.
In that case, on account of conflict, there should be an option.
Or in another performance both could be accommodated.
In the case of temporal succession, the earlier is weaker, as in the archetypal sacrifice.

6.5.s: yady udgātā jaghanyaḥ syāt punar yajñe sarvavedasaṃ dadyād yathetarasmin /
6.5.d: यद्य् उद्गाता जघन्यः स्यात् पुनर् यज्ञे सर्ववेदसं दद्याद् यथेतरस्मिन् ।
6.5.m: If the Udgātṛ should break off last, he should give all his possessions at a repeated sacrifice, just as in the other case.

6.5.s: ahargaṇe yasminn apacchedas tad āvarteta karma pṛthaktvāt /
6.5.d: अहर्गणे यस्मिन्न् अपच्छेदस् तद् आवर्तेत कर्म पृथक्त्वात् ।
6.5.m: In a multi-day sacrificial series, that rite in which the rupture occurs should be repeated, because of the distinctness of the rites.

6.6.m: When they combine, because of defectiveness, priests of equal ritual capacity should sacrifice, as in the archetypal sacrifice.
Or, by direct injunction, it should be like the head.
Not so, because it is an unattached general statement.
Or it may be [applicable], because it serves the sacrificial rite, like the Audumbarī post.
Because the Audumbarī post exists for the sake of something else, like the potsherds.
No; because of singularity, and because that other has no ritual eligibility, and because the word admits of no distinction.

6.6.s: sannipātāt tu nimittavighātaḥ syād bṛhadrathantaravad vibhaktaśiṣṭatvād vasiṣṭhanirvartye /
6.6.d: सन्निपातात् तु निमित्तविघातः स्याद् बृहद्रथन्तरवद् विभक्तशिष्टत्वाद् वसिष्ठनिर्वर्त्ये ।
6.6.m: Due to conjunction, however, there would be nullification of the occasion, as with the Bṛhat and Rathantara sāmans, because of distinct injunctions in a rite performed by a Vasiṣṭha.

6.6.s: api vā kṛtsnasaṃyogād avighātaḥ pratīyeta svāmitvenābhisaṃbandhāt /
6.6.d: अपि वा कृत्स्नसंयोगाद् अविघातः प्रतीयेत स्वामित्वेनाभिसंबन्धात् ।
6.6.m: Or rather, because of connection with the whole, non-nullification should be understood, through connection in the capacity of ownership.

6.6.s: sāmnoḥ karmavṛddhyaikadeśena saṃyoge guṇatvenābhisaṃbandhas tasmāt tatra vighātaḥ syāt /
6.6.d: साम्नोः कर्मवृद्ध्यैकदेशेन संयोगे गुणत्वेनाभिसंबन्धस् तस्मात् तत्र विघातः स्यात् ।
6.6.m: In the case of the two sāmans, because of the augmentation of the rite through connection with a part, their connection is as subordinate; therefore, in that case, there would be nullification.

6.6.s: vacanāt tu dvisaṃyogas tasmād ekasya pāṇivat /
6.6.d: वचनात् तु द्विसंयोगस् तस्माद् एकस्य पाणिवत् ।
6.6.m: By direct statement, however, there is connection with both; therefore [it is applied] to one, like the hand.
Because of absence of purpose, however, it cannot be so.

6.6.s: arthānāṃ ca vibhaktatvān na tacchrutena saṃbandhaḥ /
6.6.d: अर्थानां च विभक्तत्वान् न तच्छ्रुतेन संबन्धः ।
6.6.m: And because the purposes are distinct, there is no connection with what is directly heard in text.
Since the hand is a bodily limb, absence of connection should be recognized.
Sacrificial sessions belong to all castes without distinction.
Or rather, [they belong] to Brāhmaṇas alone, because of the absence of priestly function in the other two [castes].
No; for it is ownership that is enjoined.
Or the other two might function as the Gārhapatya, because of absence of conflict.
Because of the ownership of the others, there is the sighting of an indicative textual mark in the multi-day sacrifice.
Or [it is restricted] to the descendants of Vasiṣṭha, because of the restrictive injunction regarding the office of Brahman.
Or [it belongs] to all, because of counter-permission.
Because of the restrictive injunction that the Hotṛ must be of the Viśvāmitra family, there is no ritual eligibility for the Bhṛgus, Śunakas, and Vasiṣṭhas.
Because of the competence of the sacrificial ground, it could belong even to those without sacred fires.
And because of the prescription of an expiation.
Rather, [it belongs] to those possessing sacred fires, because it is preceded by an iṣṭi.
And because [the fires] are employed for their own purpose.
And [scripture] shows the mingling of fires.
Because the ladles and other utensils are not individually commissioned, in case of doubt, action according to desire should be recognized.

6.6.s: api vānyāni pātrāṇi sādhāraṇāni kurvīran vipratiṣedhāc chāstrakṛtvāt /
6.6.d: अपि वान्यानि पात्राणि साधारणानि कुर्वीरन् विप्रतिषेधाच् छास्त्रकृत्वात् ।
6.6.m: Or rather, they should make other utensils common, because of conflict, since it is prescribed by scripture.
In case of distress, an expiation should take place.

6.6.s: puruṣakalpena vikṛtau kartṛniyamaḥ syād yajñasya tadguṇatvād abhāvād itarān pratyekasminn adhikāraḥ syāt /
6.6.d: पुरुषकल्पेन विकृतौ कर्तृनियमः स्याद् यज्ञस्य तद्गुणत्वाद् अभावाद् इतरान् प्रत्येकस्मिन्न् अधिकारः स्यात् ।
6.6.m: By human arrangement, in an ectypal sacrifice there would be a restriction of performers, because the sacrifice has that as its secondary quality, and because in its absence, eligibility would apply to each one among the others.
And on account of textual suggestion, as in the case of a specific sacrifice.

6.6.s: na vā saṃyogapṛthaktvād guṇasyejyāpradhānatvād asaṃyuktā hi codanā /
6.6.d: न वा संयोगपृथक्त्वाद् गुणस्येज्याप्रधानत्वाद् असंयुक्ता हि चोदना ।
6.6.m: Not so, because the connection is distinct, because the secondary quality serves the sacrifice as principal, for the injunctive rule is unconnected [with that].
In the sacrifice, because it is an attribute thereof, one should restrict [it] by specific distinction.

6.7.m: In the donation of one's own property, everything [is to be given], on account of the absence of distinction.
Or rather, [only] that over which one has ownership, because the other is impossible.
It cannot be the earth, because it is undistinguished with respect to all [beings].

6.7.s: akāryatvāc ca tataḥ punar viśeṣaḥ syāt /
6.7.d: अकार्यत्वाच् च ततः पुनर् विशेषः स्यात् ।
6.7.m: And because it is not an effect, there would subsequently be a further distinction.
And because [one's own self] is permanent, there is no connection with non-permanent things.
Nor a Śūdra, because [the right to give belongs to one subject to] the scripture of duty.

6.7.s: dakṣiṇākāle yat svaṃ tat pratīyeta taddānasaṃyogāt /
6.7.d: दक्षिणाकाले यत् स्वं तत् प्रतीयेत तद्दानसंयोगात् ।
6.7.m: Whatever is one's property at the time of the sacrificial fee should be understood [as the gift], because of connection with that donation.
Because nothing is left over, the rite would conclude with that, because the rite is brought about through material substance.

6.7.s: api vā śeṣakarma syāt kratoḥ pratyakṣaśiṣṭatvāt /
6.7.d: अपि वा शेषकर्म स्यात् क्रतोः प्रत्यक्षशिष्टत्वात् ।
6.7.m: Or rather, there should be the remaining action, because the sacrificial rite is directly taught by scripture.
And likewise is the indication of another purpose seen.
However, since nothing is left over, the remaining action would be performed by accepting from someone suitable.
Because of specific mention during the consecrations, the connection is with that which does not serve the sacrificial rite; therefore there is no contradiction.

6.7.s: dīkṣāsu vinirdeśād akratvarthena saṃyogas tasmād avirodhaḥ syāt /
6.7.d: दीक्षासु विनिर्देशाद् अक्रत्वर्थेन संयोगस् तस्माद् अविरोधः स्यात् ।

6.7.s: ahargaṇe ca taddharmaḥ syāt sarveṣām aviśeṣāt /
6.7.d: अहर्गणे च तद्धर्मः स्यात् सर्वेषाम् अविशेषात् ।
6.7.m: And in an aggregate of days, its rule should apply to all, without distinction.
Or [the fee is] one hundred and twelve, as in the archetypal sacrifice.
Because it does not have that quality, it cannot be so.
Being a modification, it applies to both sides without distinction.
Or rather, [it means] something in excess, because of counter-exception.
In the case of 'unmeasured', there is prohibition of the number that is taught, because of direct scriptural statement of that.
Or rather, it is an alternative option, because it is enumerated equally.

6.7.s: adhikaṃ vā syād bahūrthatvād itareṣāṃ sannidhānāt /
6.7.d: अधिकं वा स्याद् बहूर्थत्वाद् इतरेषां सन्निधानात् ।
6.7.m: Or rather, it should be something greater, because of the meaning of 'much', and because of the proximity of the others.
And the corroborative statement serves that purpose.

6.7.s: parakṛtipurākalpaṃ ca manuṣyadharmaḥ syād arthāya hy anukīrtanam /
6.7.d: परकृतिपुराकल्पं च मनुष्यधर्मः स्याद् अर्थाय ह्य् अनुकीर्तनम् ।
6.7.m: And the deeds of another and traditional lore must be human practice, for the narration is for a purpose.
And because there is a prohibition in connection with it.
Or rather, because of specific mention, it would be a rule of that [rite], as in the case of the fivefold portioning.
In the case of an injunctive rule, however, because of connection with the Veda, it would be an authoritative instruction.

6.7.s: arthavādo vā vidhiśeṣatvāt tasmān nityānuvādaḥ syāt /
6.7.d: अर्थवादो वा विधिशेषत्वात् तस्मान् नित्यानुवादः स्यात् ।
6.7.m: Or it is a corroborative statement, because it is supplementary to an injunctive rule; therefore it would be a restatement of known fact.
A thousand-year [session] is impossible among humans, because of their lifespan.
Or rather, because of eligibility for it, it must be a human practice.

6.7.s: sa kulakalpaḥ syād iti kārṣṇājinir ekasminn asaṃbhavāt /
6.7.d: स कुलकल्पः स्याद् इति कार्ष्णाजिनिर् एकस्मिन्न् असंभवात् ।
6.7.m: It must be an arrangement by lineage—so says Kārṣṇājini—because it is impossible for a single individual.

6.7.s: api vā kṛtsnasaṃyogād ekasyaiva prayogaḥ syāt /
6.7.d: अपि वा कृत्स्नसंयोगाद् एकस्यैव प्रयोगः स्यात् ।
6.7.m: Or rather, because of connection with the whole, the performance must belong to a single person alone.

6.7.s: vipratiṣedhāt tu guṇyanyataraḥ syād iti lāvukāyanaḥ /
6.7.d: विप्रतिषेधात् तु गुण्यन्यतरः स्याद् इति लावुकायनः ।
6.7.m: However, because of conflict, one or the other subordinate factor must apply—so says Lāvukāyana.
[The word] 'year' [must be modified], because of variability.
That must be the archetypal sacrifice, because of eligibility.
Or rather, [they are] days, because of being enumerated.

6.8.s: iṣṭipūrvatvād akratuśeṣo homaḥ saṃskṛteṣv agniṣu syād pūrvo 'py ādhānasya sarvaśeṣatvāt /
6.8.d: इष्टिपूर्वत्वाद् अक्रतुशेषो होमः संस्कृतेष्व् अग्निषु स्याद् पूर्वो ऽप्य् आधानस्य सर्वशेषत्वात् ।
6.8.m: Because it is preceded by an offering, an oblation that is not supplementary to a sacrificial rite would occur in consecrated fires, even if prior, because the fire-establishment is supplementary to all [rites].

6.8.s: iṣṭitve na tu saṃstavaś caturhotṝn asaṃskṛteṣu darśayati /
6.8.d: इष्टित्वे न तु संस्तवश् चतुर्होतॄन् असंस्कृतेषु दर्शयति ।
6.8.m: However, in the status of an offering, praise shows the Caturhotṛ formulas in unconsecrated [fires].
Instruction, however, [applies here] because of transcendental potency.
Or rather, in the absence of a sacrificial rite, there is specification of what is not a supplementary element for one who has not established sacred fires.
It should be an oblation praised as an offering, because of connection with fires without context, since the others cannot be expressed.

6.8.s: iṣṭitvena saṃstute homaḥ syād anārabhyāgnisaṃyogād itareṣām avācyatvāt /
6.8.d: इष्टित्वेन संस्तुते होमः स्याद् अनारभ्याग्निसंयोगाद् इतरेषाम् अवाच्यत्वात् ।

6.8.m: Or rather, it is a specification for one who has not established fires, because of the context-free connection with fires.
In the ancestral sacrifice, there is reiteration of that which is connected.
While initiating, he should establish [the fires], because of the connection with an oblation.
Or in secular fire, as in the offering of the chieftain, because learning and rites follow a sequence.
And the establishment of fires is conjoined with a wife.

6.8.s: akarma cordhvam ādhānāt tatsamavāyo hi karmabhiḥ /
6.8.d: अकर्म चोर्ध्वम् आधानात् तत्समवायो हि कर्मभिः ।
6.8.m: And there is no ritual action before the establishment of fires, for association with ritual actions belongs [only] to that.
[No,] because there would be a conflict with direct scriptural statement.
And because [the fires] serve all [rites], a rite aimed at [obtaining] a son cannot instigate [the laying of the fires].

6.8.s: somapānāt tu prāpaṇaṃ dvitīyasya tasmād upayacchet /
6.8.d: सोमपानात् तु प्रापणं द्वितीयस्य तस्माद् उपयच्छेत् ।
6.8.m: But [the second wife is to be taken] because drinking Soma requires the presence of a second [wife]; therefore he should marry [another].

6.8.s: pitṛyajñe tu darśanāt prāg ādhānāt pratīyeta /
6.8.d: पितृयज्ञे तु दर्शनात् प्राग् आधानात् प्रतीयेत ।
6.8.m: In the rite to the ancestors, however, because of its being observed [as prior], it should be understood as occurring before the laying of the fires.

6.8.s: sthapatīṣṭiḥ prayājavad agnayādheyaṃ prayojayet tādarthyāc cāpavṛjyeta /
6.8.d: स्थपतीष्टिः प्रयाजवद् अग्नयाधेयं प्रयोजयेत् तादर्थ्याच् चापवृज्येत ।
6.8.m: [In the view of the opponent:] The sacrifice of the chieftain, like the fore-sacrifices, would instigate the laying of the fires, and [the fires] would cease [afterwards] because they exist for that purpose.

6.8.d: अपि वा लौकिके ऽग्नौ स्याद् आधानस्यासर्वशेषत्वात् ।
6.8.m: Or rather, it should take place in the worldly fire, because the laying [of the fires] is not subordinate to all [persons].
And the animal sacrifice of the student who has broken his vow of chastity is likewise, because the time for laying the fires has not arrived.
Rites to the gods based on tradition take place during the northern course of the sun, the waxing fortnight of the month, and auspicious days, because of indications of purpose.
And during the day is the completeness of the ritual action.
Begging or purchasing [takes place] when [the prescribed substance is] absent, as in worldly affairs.
Or it must be restricted, because it has an effective purpose.
Likewise regarding the consumption, summons, covering, immolation, offering, and aversion.
What is devoid of purpose, however, would be non-obligatory.
In the injunction regarding an animal, there is no restriction, because there is no specification.

6.8.s: niyamo vaikārthyaṃ hy arthabhedād bhedaḥ pṛthavatvenābhidhānāt /
6.8.d: नियमो वैकार्थ्यं ह्य् अर्थभेदाद् भेदः पृथवत्वेनाभिधानात् ।
6.8.m: Or there is restriction, for there is identity of purpose; difference [arises] from a difference of purpose, because it is designated as having a distinct character.
Or there is no restriction, because it is a different meaning; difference [is established] through distinct words of exclusion.
In the case of the goat, it is not the name of the ritual action, because of its form and indicative textual mark.
Because its form is different, it cannot be a word denoting a genus.
It is not a modification, because the relation is primordial.
That [quality] is accidental, because the qualification of the animal is not enjoined.
Or it denotes the genus, because of the frequent usage and its purposeful meaning.

7.1.s: śrutipramāṇatvāc cheṣāṇāṃ mukhyabhede yathādhikāraṃ bhāvaḥ syāt /
7.1.d: श्रुतिप्रमाणत्वाच् छेषाणां मुख्यभेदे यथाधिकारं भावः स्यात् ।
7.1.m: Because direct scriptural statement is the means of valid cognition, when the primary elements differ, the state of the subsidiaries must correspond to each ritual eligibility.
Or, because the origination and purpose are undivided, they would share the same ritual procedure, as in the case of individual substances.

7.1.s: codanāśeṣabhāvād vā tadbhedād vyavatiṣṭherann utpatter guṇabhūtatvāt /
7.1.d: चोदनाशेषभावाद् वा तद्भेदाद् व्यवतिष्ठेरन्न् उत्पत्तेर् गुणभूतत्वात् ।
7.1.m: Or, because they are subsidiaries of the injunction, they would be distributed according to its differences, since the origination is secondary.
If it were an entity, on account of the connection with the defining characteristic, it would be understood as applying universally.
Because there is no distinction, however, it cannot be so.
And having two purposes is contradictory.

7.1.s: utpattau vidhyabhāvād vā codanāyāṃ pravṛttiḥ syāt tataś ca karmabhedaḥ syāt /
7.1.d: उत्पत्तौ विध्यभावाद् वा चोदनायां प्रवृत्तिः स्यात् ततश् च कर्मभेदः स्यात् ।
7.1.m: Or because there is no injunctive rule in the origination, the application would be in the injunction, and hence there would be difference of ritual action.

7.1.s: yadi vāpy abhidhānavat sāmānyāt sarvadharmaḥ syāt /
7.1.d: यदि वाप्य् अभिधानवत् सामान्यात् सर्वधर्मः स्यात् ।
7.1.m: Or, as in the case of designations, on account of similarity, all ritual properties would apply.

7.1.s: arthasya tv avibhaktatvāt tathā syād abhidhāneṣu pūrvavattvāt prayogasya karmaṇaḥ śabdabhāvyatvād vibhāgāc cheṣāṇām apravṛttiḥ syāt /
7.1.d: अर्थस्य त्व् अविभक्तत्वात् तथा स्याद् अभिधानेषु पूर्ववत्त्वात् प्रयोगस्य कर्मणः शब्दभाव्यत्वाद् विभागाच् छेषाणाम् अप्रवृत्तिः स्यात् ।
7.1.m: Because the purpose is undivided, it would be so; in designations, because performance has a precedent, because the ritual action is brought into being by the verbal testimony, and because of distinction, there would be no application of the subsidiaries.

7.1.s: arthasya śabdabhāvyatvāt prakaraṇanibandhanāc chabdād evānyatra bhāvaḥ syāt /
7.1.d: अर्थस्य शब्दभाव्यत्वात् प्रकरणनिबन्धनाच् छब्दाद् एवान्यत्र भावः स्यात् ।
7.1.m: Because the purpose is brought into being by verbal testimony, on account of its connection to the context of the ritual topic, its existence elsewhere could only be from direct verbal statement.
In what is common, because it has a precedent, the ritual eligibility would belong to what has originated.

7.1.s: api vā yady apūrvatvād itaradadhikārthe jyautiṣṭomikād vidhes tadvācakaṃ samānaṃ syāt /
7.1.d: अपि वा यद्य् अपूर्वत्वाद् इतरदधिकार्थे ज्यौतिष्टोमिकाद् विधेस् तद्वाचकं समानं स्यात् ।
7.1.m: Or, if on account of being an unexampled rite the other serves a further purpose, the expression denoting it would be identical with that of the injunctive rule of the Jyotiṣṭoma.
In the five recurrent offerings, there is extended application of the corroborative statement because of proximity.
Or of all, because of identity of verbal expression.
And the cake on one potsherd and the cake to Indra-Agni are likewise.

7.1.s: ekakapālānāṃ vaiśvadevikaḥ prakṛtir āgrayaṇe sarvahomāparivṛttidarśanād avabhṛthe ca sakṛd dvyavadānasya vacanāt /
7.1.d: एककपालानां वैश्वदेविकः प्रकृतिर् आग्रयणे सर्वहोमापरिवृत्तिदर्शनाद् अवभृथे च सकृद् द्व्यवदानस्य वचनात् ।
7.1.m: For the single-potsherd cakes, the Vaiśvadeva rite is the archetypal sacrifice, because in the Āgrayaṇa offering no complete offering [of all parts] is seen, and because at the Avabhṛtha bath there is an express statement of taking two portions at once.

7.2.m: The application of a Sāman chant would occur by means of its proper name, as instructed.

7.2.s: śabdais tv arthavidhitvād arthāntare 'pravṛttiḥ syāt pṛthagbhāvāt kriyāyā hy abhisambandhaḥ /
7.2.d: शब्दैस् त्व् अर्थविधित्वाद् अर्थान्तरे ऽप्रवृत्तिः स्यात् पृथग्भावात् क्रियाया ह्य् अभिसम्बन्धः ।
7.2.m: By words, however, because they enjoin the purpose, there would be no application to another purpose, because of their separate nature; for the connection is indeed with the action.

7.2.s: svārthe vā syāt prayojanaṃ kriyāyās tadaṅgabhāvenopadiśyeran /
7.2.d: स्वार्थे वा स्यात् प्रयोजनं क्रियायास् तदङ्गभावेनोपदिश्येरन् ।
7.2.m: Or its utility lies in its own purpose; [the words] would be taught as subsidiaries of that action.
And in this way scripture would be devoid of purpose.
[We reply:] No, because of the absence of purpose, there is no connection with direct scriptural statement.
The accent, however, would belong to the original forms, because it is undivided from the mora and the phoneme.
But because there is no direct scriptural statement of modification in the subsequent [verses], [the tone is] according to direct scriptural statement.
And [otherwise there would be] an inconsistency of the words.

7.2.s: api tu karmaśabdaḥ syād bhāvo 'rthaḥ prasiddhagrahaṇatvād vikāro hy aviśiṣṭo 'nyaiḥ /
7.2.d: अपि तु कर्मशब्दः स्याद् भावो ऽर्थः प्रसिद्धग्रहणत्वाद् विकारो ह्य् अविशिष्टो ऽन्यैः ।
7.2.m: On the contrary, it must be a word expressive of action, its object being an act, because it is grasped as well-known; for modification is not distinct from the others.

7.2.s: tasya ca kriyā grahaṇārthā nānārtheṣu virūpitvād artho hy āsāmalaukiko vidhānāt /
7.2.d: तस्य च क्रिया ग्रहणार्था नानार्थेषु विरूपित्वाद् अर्थो ह्य् आसामलौकिको विधानात् ।
7.2.m: And its performance is for the purpose of acquisition, because of diversity in different purposes; for their purpose is non-empirical, by virtue of injunction.
In respect of that, there must be specific designations, because of the distinctness of the modifications.
And the verses in the matrix-hymns are enjoined equally with the other [verses].
And also, in that which is not a matrix, [a chant] is seen which does not have that matrix.
If it is said that, where there is a single purpose, there is no diversity of form;
[we reply that] it could be, because in the case of other purposes there is no accomplishment, as in cooking.
And [thus] there is consistency of the words.

7.3.s: uktaṃ kriyābhidhānaṃ tacchrutāv anyatra vidhipradeśaḥ syāt /
7.3.d: उक्तं क्रियाभिधानं तच्छ्रुताव् अन्यत्र विधिप्रदेशः स्यात् ।
7.3.m: The designation of the action has been stated; when it is heard, there would be an extension of injunctive rule elsewhere.
But because the name is innate;

7.3.s: pratyakṣād guṇasaṃyogāt kriyābhidhānaṃ syāt tadabhāve 'prasiddhaṃ syāt /
7.3.d: प्रत्यक्षाद् गुणसंयोगात् क्रियाभिधानं स्यात् तदभावे ऽप्रसिद्धं स्यात् ।
7.3.m: from direct perception, through connection with a secondary quality, it would be the designation of an action; in its absence, it would be unknown.

7.3.s: api vā satrakarmaṇi guṇārthaiṣā śrutiḥ syāt /
7.3.d: अपि वा सत्रकर्मणि गुणार्थैषा श्रुतिः स्यात् ।
7.3.m: Or rather, in the ritual of a sacrificial session, this direct scriptural statement would be for the sake of a secondary quality.

7.3.s: viśvajiti sarvapṛṣṭhe tatpūrvakatvāj jyautiṣṭomikāni pṛṣṭhāny asti ca pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ /
7.3.d: विश्वजिति सर्वपृष्ठे तत्पूर्वकत्वाज् ज्यौतिष्टोमिकानि पृष्ठान्य् अस्ति च पृष्ठशब्दः ।
7.3.m: In the Viśvajit, which has all the Pṛṣṭhas, because it is preceded by it, the Pṛṣṭhas are those pertaining to the Jyotiṣṭoma rite, and there is the word ‘Pṛṣṭha’.
Or from the six-day rite, for the injunction is there.
The Jyotiṣṭoma rite has its ritual eligibility already established.
not so, because the word ‘all’ would be meaningless.

7.3.s: dravyādeśe taddravyaḥ śrutisaṃyogāt puroḍāśas tv anādeśe tatprakṛtitvāt /
7.3.d: द्रव्यादेशे तद्द्रव्यः श्रुतिसंयोगात् पुरोडाशस् त्व् अनादेशे तत्प्रकृतित्वात् ।
7.3.m: When a substance is specified, it has that substance, because of connection with direct scriptural statement; but the sacrificial cake [is used] when there is no specification, because it is its archetypal sacrifice.
An injunctive rule of a secondary quality, however, would not adopt [it], because of equality.
And so it is in the case of the churned fire, and the like.
The bringing forward, however, is that belonging to the Soma rite, for the other is not expressible.
And the negative prohibition of the high altar is likewise.
[we reply:] the audible mention is for the purpose of exclusive specification, or for a secondary quality, or [it is] a corroborative statement.
The bringing forward is in the first and last [sacrifices], because of the negative prohibition of the high altar.
Or in the two middle ones, because of an explanatory praise of movement.
The negative prohibition of that which relates to the high altar belongs to an unattached statement.
And [so it is with] the Svarasāman, the single-cup offering, and the curd mixture, because of the observation of an indicative textual mark.
Or the form, because it is an auxiliary part.
In case of doubt, it must be worldly, because it serves all purposes.
It cannot be Vedic, because of the specification of purpose.
So also the origination of the others, because of equality.
It must be consecrated, because it has that word.
Or figuratively, because it is not an accessory to the sacrifice, since qualities are designated.
The word ‘Pṛṣṭha’ must apply to the ritual action, because it is taught as being such.

7.3.s: abhidhānopadeśād vā vipratiṣedhād dravyeṣu pṛṣṭhaśabdaḥ syāt /
7.3.d: अभिधानोपदेशाद् वा विप्रतिषेधाद् द्रव्येषु पृष्ठशब्दः स्यात् ।
7.3.m: Or, because of the teaching of the designation, the word ‘Pṛṣṭha’ would apply to the substances on account of contradiction.

7.4.m: Because of the injunctive rule of modal procedure, the sacrifice has that which preceded it.
It would be worldly, because its operation is seen.
By virtue of Vedic statement, however, it is different from that.
Or it should be restricted by an indicative textual mark, because an indicative textual mark is a subordinate quality of it.
Or rather, because it is preceded by illogicality where there are statements that are permanent reiterations.

7.4.s: mitho vipratiṣedhāc ca guṇānāṃ yathārthatalpanā syāt /
7.4.d: मिथो विप्रतिषेधाच् च गुणानां यथार्थतल्पना स्यात् ।
7.4.m: And because of mutual contradiction, the assumption of secondary qualities would be according to the purpose.

7.4.s: bhāgitvāt tu niyamyeta guṇānām abhidhānatvāt sambandhād abhidhānavad yathā dhenuḥ kiśoreṇa /
7.4.d: भागित्वात् तु नियम्येत गुणानाम् अभिधानत्वात् सम्बन्धाद् अभिधानवद् यथा धेनुः किशोरेण ।
7.4.m: It must, however, be restricted because it is a recipient, since qualities are designations, as a designation by virtue of connection, like a cow by her calf.

7.4.s: utpattīnāṃ samatvād vā yathādhikāraṃ bhāvaḥ syāt /
7.4.d: उत्पत्तीनां समत्वाद् वा यथाधिकारं भावः स्यात् ।
7.4.m: Or, because originations are equal, the presence would be according to ritual eligibility.
And the statement of origination and auxiliary is contradictory in one [and the same rite].

7.4.s: vidhyanto vā prakṛtivac codanāyāṃ pravarteta tathā hi liṅgadarśanam /
7.4.d: विध्यन्तो वा प्रकृतिवच् चोदनायां प्रवर्तेत तथा हि लिङ्गदर्शनम् ।
7.4.m: Or the ritual details would operate in the injunction like the archetypal sacrifice; for thus is the observation of an indicative textual mark.
Because the indicative textual mark is the cause, in the absence of an indicative textual mark it would be worldly.

7.4.s: liṅgasya pūrvavattavāc codanāśabdasāmānyād ekenāpi nirūpyeta yathā sthālīpulākena /
7.4.d: लिङ्गस्य पूर्ववत्तवाच् चोदनाशब्दसामान्याद् एकेनापि निरूप्येत यथा स्थालीपुलाकेन ।
7.4.m: Because the indicative textual mark has a precedent, and because of the commonness of the injunctive word, it could be ascertained even by a single one, as [the boiling of rice in] a pot by a single grain.

7.4.s: dvādaśāhikam ahargaṇe tatprakṛtitvād aikāhikam adhikāgamāt tadākhyaṃ syād ekāhavat /
7.4.d: द्वादशाहिकम् अहर्गणे तत्प्रकृतित्वाद् ऐकाहिकम् अधिकागमात् तदाख्यं स्याद् एकाहवत् ।
7.4.m: In a group of days, that which belongs to the twelve-day rite [is extended], because it is its archetypal sacrifice; that which belongs to the one-day rite [is extended only] when there is an additional factor; it would have that name like a one-day rite.
Or rather not so, because [the term] designates a sacrificial rite, and the excess [days] are not expressed by the word.
The indicative textual mark would belong to the aggregate, because the purpose applies to that, just as in the case of a substance.
Or rather not so, because properties belong to the purpose, the aggregate being secondary.
In the case of substances, the attainment of properties would occur because the purpose applies [to them].
There is perception of an indicative textual mark of that which is restricted by the performance.
The mention of the distribution of sacred fires refers to what is qualified, because statements not commenced under a specific topic apply to the archetypal sacrifice.

8.1.m: [The property belongs to that rite] whose indicative textual mark [is found], on account of connection with the purpose, just as with a designation.
Because it is a performance, there would be application of the [archetypal] iṣṭi in the Soma sacrifice.
Or rather, [the Soma sacrifice] has a transcendental potency of its own, because of its complete injunction.
And because the absence of besprinkling the ladle is an obligatory restatement.
There is perception of the [properties] of the iṣṭi.
There should be the application of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices to [other] iṣṭis.
And because an indicative textual mark is observed in the animal sacrifice.
In the eleven animal sacrifices, [the archetype is] the animal sacrifice of the Soma-pressing day, because of the observation of two ropes.
Its application should be in groups [of sacrifices], because a sacrificial post is observed for each animal.
And in group-series rites, the application of the prior should be in the subsequent ones.

8.1.s: karmaṇas tv apravṛttitvāt phalaniyamakartṛ samudāyasyānanvayas tadbandhanatvāt /
8.1.d: कर्मणस् त्व् अप्रवृत्तित्वात् फलनियमकर्तृ समुदायस्यानन्वयस् तद्बन्धनत्वात् ।
8.1.m: But because the ritual action does not transfer, the collection of fruit, restriction, and agent does not connect, because it is bound to that [original rite].
And even if it were to transfer, [it would not connect] because it is for the sake of that [archetype].
In optional secondary elements, there would be application, because they are based [on the action].
Or rather, there is non-application, on account of the difference in ritual actions.
Or rather, because it is not a modification thereof and because it serves the sacrificial rite, application would take place.
In a single ritual action there is alternative adoption, for there is no distinction, because the injunction is one.
There would be alternative adoption on account of the commonality of the indicative textual mark.

8.1.s: aikārthyād vā niyamyeta pūrvavattvād vikāro hi /
8.1.d: ऐकार्थ्याद् वा नियम्येत पूर्ववत्त्वाद् विकारो हि ।
8.1.m: Or rather, it should be restricted by unity of purpose, for a modified rite possesses [properties] like the prior [archetype].
And likewise, there is observation of another purpose.
In case of conflict, it should be restricted by the sacrificial offering, because the ritual action is named after it.
The direct scriptural mention of the deity is by way of a subordinate qualification.
Gold has the properties of clarified butter, because of brilliance.
Or rather, it is [a modification of] vegetable oblation, because of solidity.
And because cooking is directly heard in scriptural text regarding it.
In the case of honey-water, it should be a modification of milk, on account of the commonality of substance.
Or rather clarified butter, on account of the commonality of color.
And because the former has no specific distinction.

8.2.s: vājine somapūrvatvaṃ sautrāmaṇyāñ ca graheṣu tācchabdyāt /
8.2.d: वाजिने सोमपूर्वत्वं सौत्रामण्याञ् च ग्रहेषु ताच्छब्द्यात् ।
8.2.m: In the case of whey, and in the Sautrāmaṇī cups, the Soma sacrifice is the prior [archetype], on account of the use of that word.
And on account of consuming after an invitation.
And purchasing, cooking, reciting the introductory verse, holding in a vessel, placing, and wrapping in cloth are likewise.
Or rather, it should be restricted by the sacrificial offering, because it is a modification thereof.
And there is observation of an indicative textual mark of the animal-cake offering.
The animal offering should be a modification of the sacrificial cake, on account of the commonality of deity.
Rather, [the animal offering is a modification of] the curd-and-milk oblation, because of originating from it;
And because its vessel is observed [in the ritual texts];
[It should be a modification] of the curd, on account of the common property of solid form;
The curdled milk clot (āmikṣā), because it is produced from both, should be a modification of both;
Because of the common property of solidity with curd;

8.2.s: payo vā tatpradhānatvāl lokavad dadhnas tadarthatvāt /
8.2.d: पयो वा तत्प्रधानत्वाल् लोकवद् दध्नस् तदर्थत्वात् ।
8.2.m: Or [a modification] of milk, because that is the principal constituent, as in worldly matters, since curd exists for the sake of it;

8.2.s: satramahīnaś ca dvādaśāhas tasyobhayathā pravṛttir aikakarmyāt /
8.2.d: सत्रमहीनश् च द्वादशाहस् तस्योभयथा प्रवृत्तिर् ऐककर्म्यात् ।
8.2.m: The twelve-day rite is both a sacrificial session and a multi-day sacrifice: its application is twofold, because of its identical performance;

8.2.s: api vā yajatiśruter ahīnabhūtapravṛttiḥ syāt prakṛtyā tulya śabdatvāt /
8.2.d: अपि वा यजतिश्रुतेर् अहीनभूतप्रवृत्तिः स्यात् प्रकृत्या तुल्य शब्दत्वात् ।
8.2.m: Rather, by the direct scriptural statement of the verb 'he sacrifices' (yajati), it functions as a multi-day sacrifice, because the wording is equal to the archetypal sacrifice;
[The rites] from the two-day up to the eleven-day rite have the character of a multi-day sacrifice, because of the injunction with the verb 'he sacrifices' (yajati);
In rites of thirteen days and upward, it has the nature of a sacrificial session, because in them there is the injunction of 'sitting' and 'undertaking';

8.2.s: anyatarato 'tirātratvāt pañcadaśarātrasyāhīnatvaṃ kuṇḍapāyināmayanasya ca tadbhūteṣv ahīnatvasya darśanāt /
8.2.d: अन्यतरतो ऽतिरात्रत्वात् पञ्चदशरात्रस्याहीनत्वं कुण्डपायिनामयनस्य च तद्भूतेष्व् अहीनत्वस्य दर्शनात् ।
8.2.m: The fifteen-day rite and the Kuṇḍapāyins' session have the nature of a multi-day sacrifice because there is an Atirātra at only one end, and because the nature of a multi-day sacrifice is seen in rites of that type;
And [scripture] displays an indicative textual mark of a sacrificial session;

8.3.m: In a group of sacrificial offerings, the subsequent one [follows the archetypal details] of the subsequent, because of the common spatial order;
Or it should be determined by the recipient deity, because of verbal expression, while the other [relation] is not directly stated by scriptural text;
When a group [of days] is enjoined, repetition should be understood of that [day] whose indicative textual mark is present, as in the case of the Āgneya;
Or [they are] distinct days, because of being an aggregate, since the injunction is accompanied by the indicative textual mark of continuous progression;
And thus another purpose is seen [in the texts];
Even when there is repetition of the time, [there are distinct days], so says Bādari, because of difference in ritual action;
Jaimini, however, [holds that] it is repetition of that [same rite], because the number of days is not directly perceived;
In groups of soma-terminations, repetition of that [same archetype] should be understood, because an established characteristic is apprehended;

8.3.s: adhikārād vā prakṛtis tadviśiṣṭā syād abhidhānasya tannimittatvāt /
8.3.d: अधिकाराद् वा प्रकृतिस् तद्विशिष्टा स्याद् अभिधानस्य तन्निमित्तत्वात् ।
8.3.m: Or, by virtue of ritual eligibility, the archetypal sacrifice must be differentiated by that [order], because the naming is caused by that;
The accumulation [of days] is derived from the group [of days], because that is its archetypal base;
Or [it is derived] from the one-day rite, because they are equal;

8.3.s: gāyatrīṣu prākṛtīnām avacchedaḥ prakṛtyādhikārāt saṃkhyātvād agniṣṭomavad avyatirekāt tadākhyatvam /
8.3.d: गायत्रीषु प्राकृतीनाम् अवच्छेदः प्रकृत्याधिकारात् संख्यात्वाद् अग्निष्टोमवद् अव्यतिरेकात् तदाख्यत्वम् ।
8.3.m: In the case of the Gāyatrī verses, there is a limitation of the archetypal verses, because of the context of the archetype, because of the number, and because, as in the case of the Agniṣṭoma, it is named after it due to non-difference;
And because it is regularly mentioned, that statement applies to distinct verses;
Or the word for the substance denotes a secondary quality, because it does not apply to all;
And there is coordination, as in the case of the cow-genus;
And because the number is verbally expressed;
Because it does not reside in another substance, it would be differentiated by the omissions of the Ukthya;
And because it is not characterized by scriptural teaching;
Because it is an originary proper name, it would apply figuratively to distinct verses;

8.3.s: apūrve ca vikalpaḥ syād yadi saṃkhyāvidhānam /
8.3.d: अपूर्वे च विकल्पः स्याद् यदि संख्याविधानम् ।
8.3.m: And with regard to what is novel, there would be an option if it were the injunction of a number;
If it be objected that it is not so, because an already established [object] is apprehended;

8.3.s: yadi vāviśaye niyamaḥ prakṛtyupabandhāc chareṣv api prasiddhaḥ syāt /
8.3.d: यदि वाविशये नियमः प्रकृत्युपबन्धाच् छरेष्व् अपि प्रसिद्धः स्यात् ।
8.3.m: If there were a restrictive rule in an ambiguous case, it would also be established in the case of reed grass, because of the connection with the archetype;

8.3.s: arthasya cāsamāptatvān na tāsām ekadeśe syāt /
8.3.d: अर्थस्य चासमाप्तत्वान् न तासाम् एकदेशे स्यात् ।
8.3.m: And because the purpose is not completed, it cannot apply to a single part of them;

8.4.m: The ladle-homa (darvihoma) is the name of a sacrifice, because of its connection with the word 'homa';
It must belong to worldly rites, because the agent is named by that [designation].
Or rather, [it applies] to all, because it is seen in the Vāstuhoma.
Or rather, [it applies] to the injunctions with juhoti, because of connection with that.
Or rather, because of the teaching of the substance, it should be an expression of an accessory.
Not of worldly [rites], because of relying on traditional custom, and because what is accompanied by Vedic words is enjoined for another purpose.
And because of the observation of a different vessel.
And the relation to the purpose has been stated.
In that case, Soma would apply, because it is unmanifest.

8.4.s: na vā svāhākāreṇa saṃyogād vāṣaṭkārasya ca nirdeśāt tantretena vipratiṣedhāt /
8.4.d: न वा स्वाहाकारेण संयोगाद् वाषट्कारस्य च निर्देशात् तन्त्रेतेन विप्रतिषेधात् ।
8.4.m: Not so, because of the connection with the svāhā-call, and because of the mention of the vaṣaṭ-call, through the procedure [of the archetypal rite] there would be contradiction with it.

8.4.s: uttarārthas tu svāhākāro yathā sāptadaśyaṃ tatrāvipratiṣiddhā punaḥ pravṛttir liṅgadarśanāt paśuvat /
8.4.d: उत्तरार्थस् तु स्वाहाकारो यथा साप्तदश्यं तत्राविप्रतिषिद्धा पुनः प्रवृत्तिर् लिङ्गदर्शनात् पशुवत् ।
8.4.m: However, the svāhā-call is for the subsequent rite, like the seventeen-fold state; its recurring application there is not contradictory, because of seeing an indicative textual mark, as in the case of the animal [sacrifice].

8.4.s: anuttarārtho vārthavattvād ānarthakyād dhi prākṛtasyoparodhaḥ syāt /
8.4.d: अनुत्तरार्थो वार्थवत्त्वाद् आनर्थक्याद् धि प्राकृतस्योपरोधः स्यात् ।
8.4.m: Or rather, it is not for a subsequent rite, because of having its own purpose; for from purposelessness there would be the obstruction of the archetypal [element].
The subsequent weakness in co-occurrence has been stated.
Or rather, its injunction would be an injunctive rule, because the iṣṭi is already established in application.
Because the absence [of an archetype] is the reason there, non-perception would be for the sake of an accessory.

8.4.s: na vākyaśeṣatvād guṇārthe ca samādhānaṃ nānātvenopapadyate /
8.4.d: न वाक्यशेषत्वाद् गुणार्थे च समाधानं नानात्वेनोपपद्यते ।
8.4.m: No, because it is the remainder of a sentence, and a conciliation for the sake of an accessory is established through diversity.

8.4.s: yeṣāṃ vāparayor hemas teṣāṃ syād avirodhāt /
8.4.d: येषां वापरयोर् हेमस् तेषां स्याद् अविरोधात् ।
8.4.m: Or rather, for those whose offering is in the other two [fires], [it belongs] to them, because of non-contradiction.
Herbs are enjoined there; they would be understood by spatial order.

8.4.s:
pratipatti tu te bhavatas tasmād atādvikāratvam /
sannipāte virodhinām apravṛttiḥ pratīyeta vidhyutpattivyavasthānād arthasyāpariṇeyatvād vacanād atideśaḥ syāt /
8.4.d:
प्रतिपत्ति तु ते भवतस् तस्माद् अताद्विकारत्वम् ।
सन्निपाते विरोधिनाम् अप्रवृत्तिः प्रतीयेत विध्युत्पत्तिव्यवस्थानाद् अर्थस्यापरिणेयत्वाद् वचनाद् अतिदेशः स्यात् ।
8.4.m:
However, those two are disposal rites; therefore there is absence of modification from that.

In the clash of conflicting elements, non-application would be recognized, because of the settlement of origin by injunctive rule; because the purpose cannot be transposed, extended application would be [only] by explicit statement.
